subject: Incident: multi-region cloud outage — routing guidance & post-incident plan
messages:
From: ops@acme-corp.com
To: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: alex@acme-corp.com
Date: Wed, 08 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Urgent] API errors and increased latency in US/EU regions

Marcus —

Heads up: starting ~08:45 PDT we're seeing a spike in 500s and timeouts from Redwood endpoints for our users routed to us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Latency jumped from ~80ms to >1.5s and several longer requests just failed. We've tried reissuing requests a few times; same result.

Impact: our search embeddings and chat features are affected for ~12% of active sessions. We have a handful of high-priority users on a live demo right now.

Can you confirm whether this is Redwood-side? If so, any immediate mitigation we can apply (regional reroute, model fallback, or a config toggle)? We need an ETA and guidance to keep the demo alive.

Attachments: sample-request-log.txt (text)

— Alex
Alex Chen
Ops Lead, ACME Corporation
alex@acme-corp.com

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: ops@acme-corp.com, alex@acme-corp.com
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 08 Apr 2026 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [Urgent] API errors and increased latency in US/EU regions

Alex — thanks for the report and the logs. We're seeing elevated error rates originating from a subset of our hosted nodes that are in the provider's us-east and eu-west regions. Engineering has confirmed this looks like a provider-side network flap affecting control-plane-to-data-plane routing; tokens and KV caches are intact.

Immediate guidance (what to try now):
- Quickest: set your client to prefer the ap-south-1 or us-west-2 region until the provider stabilizes. Example (curl):
  curl https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate?region=us-west-2 \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-large","input":"..."}'
- Alternate: add "fallback_model=rwd-medium" parameter for shorter requests which reduces chance of hitting the impacted pool.
- If you have dedicated capacity with us, switch routing to your dedicated endpoint: https://dedicated-usX.redwood.com (contact me if you need the exact host).

We pushed a temporary routing rule to avoid the affected nodes and are monitoring. That will reduce throughput for a short window, but should cut the 500s. I'll keep you updated every 30 minutes.

Attachments: routing-runbook-v2.pdf (excerpt with curl snippets)

— Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198

I'll take the external sync with ACME at the 10:30AM PT checkpoint. Please update the doc and paste links in Slack #incidents.

Subject: Final update: outage resolved in affected regions + postmortem link

Alex / ACME team —

Follow-up from our on-call and provider communications: the provider resolved the control-plane routing issue in us-east-1 and eu-west-1 at ~2026-04-08T22:18:00Z. Our temporary routing rule was removed at 22:45Z after validation. You may see cached DNS propagation for a short window; normal latency and error rates returned for your traffic by ~22:50Z.

What happened (short summary for customers):
- An upstream cloud-networking control-plane disruption caused intermittent routing failures for a subset of instances in us-east-1 and eu-west-1.
- Redwood applied a temporary regional routing policy and offered customers the option to swap to dedicated endpoints or alternate regions to restore service quickly.

What we've done for ACME:
- Provided immediate reroute instructions (ap-south-1 / us-west-2) and a fallback model parameter.
- Confirmed your live demo completed once routing was applied.
- Preparing a postmortem and proposed credits; draft is linked below.

Postmortem (draft): https://drive.redwood.com/incident/ACME-2026-04-08-postmortem
HubSpot ticket: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/ACME-12345/ticket/67890

Next steps (internal):
- Runbook update: ensure regional health-checks include control-plane reachability steps (owner: Monica).
- Permanently add the temporary routing rule as an automated fallback for short windows (owner: Grace/Dylan).
- Customer communication: Evelyn to finalize external note and schedule a sync with ACME next week to walk through the RCA.

As a courtesy for the customer impact, our account team will propose a single-month credit against April usage on ACME's account; I'll coordinate with finance.

Thanks for your patience and for flagging this quickly. Please reply if you see any lingering issues.

— Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
